_comment: DRC negative control for layout/sampling-frontend/bin/run-flow.sh: a
deliberately illegal n-well fixture that `klt drc --deck sky130` must
report as VIOLATIONS, naming nwell.space.1 and nwell.width.1.
Why a well fixture specifically. This sub-block's whole PFET body-tie
story (DR-004 / DR-007) is a deliberate n-well SPLIT into three
electrically distinct islands, so 'the composed layout is DRC-clean'
means nothing unless the deck being run can actually see an illegal well
spacing. Until klt 0.4.0 it could not: klt 0.3.0's curated sky130 rule
table carried NO rules on layer 64 at all, which is why
layout/sampling-frontend-wells/ (issue #122) had to ship a
hand-transcribed `drc/nwell_isolation.drc` and run it through
`klt drc --engine klayout --deck-file`. klt 0.4.0 closed that gap
upstream (klayout-tools#1420) by adding nwell.width.1 and nwell.space.1
to the curated deck, so this flow runs the fixture through the SAME
curated deck the deliverable is checked against -- no parallel rule
transcription to maintain, and no dependency on a `klayout` binary.
Defects, spaced far enough apart that each fires exactly one rule:
nwell.space.1  two 2.0 x 2.0 um nwell islands 0.50 um apart -- below
the 1.27 um minimum, i.e. the exact failure mode a
deliberately-split well risks (physically ONE merged
well on silicon, and therefore one body net, while the
drawn geometry still looks like two).
nwell.width.1  a 0.60 um wide nwell stripe -- below the 0.84 um
minimum.
The last two shape groups (a tap coincident with its nwell, and a diff
coincident with its nwell -- both 0 um enclosure, below the 0.18 um
difftap.10 / difftap.8 minima) are drawn but are NOT expected to be
flagged: klt 0.4.0's curated deck deliberately does not transcribe those
two rules, because sky130 scopes them by the nsdm/psdm implant markers
no `klt gen` generator draws. They are kept here so the record's own
rule_counts document, reproducibly, exactly which well-family rules the
deck does and does not carry -- rather than that gap living only in
prose. See README.md, 'What this flow does not check'.
Written with `klt draw`, which writes geometry verbatim with no rule
checking -- exactly what a DRC negative control needs, the same way
layout/bin/drc_violation_fixture.json is the negative control for the
trivial-cell flow's own curated-deck verdict.
Geometry re-used from layout/sampling-frontend-wells/drc/
nwell_isolation_fixture.json (issue #122), which established this
fixture's shape for the same well-split claim.
